Chapter 95: They're All My Workers

Peking University's Yuanhuo Club was founded in 1998, making it one of the earlier university animation societies.

Unlike its later scale of two to three thousand people, it only had about a hundred members at this time.

When she heard Chen Guiliang wanted to hire people to draw original art, the senior sister was first taken aback, then smiled and said, "Junior brother, you can join our Yuanhuo Club first. Once you're one of us, we can discuss anything."

"Give me the application form." Chen Guiliang readily accepted.

A senior brother sitting at a table said, "Junior brother, come over, sit down, and fill out the form."

While filling out the application form to join the club, Chen Guiliang chatted with these senior brothers and sisters.

The four people before him were three sophomores and one junior, from different departments.

The senior sister who had just spoken to Chen Guiliang was named Guo Caicai. The other three were named Li Hang, Zeng Hui, and Sheng Qingchuan.

They were all core members of the Yuanhuo Club.

Among them, Li Hang was a computer science major who was also skilled at drawing with Photoshop 7.0. This was considered high-end tech in 2004, as most artists were still drawing by hand on paper.

Once Chen Guiliang paid the fee and joined the club, he was considered one of their own.

Guo Caicai asked, "Junior brother, what do you want to draw?"

Chen Guiliang had only left written materials at the Peking University Science Park; he had the simple Legends of the Three Kingdoms cards with him. "Let's play cards first."

A few minutes later, the five of them were gathered around the table playing Legends of the Three Kingdoms.

As they were getting into the game, a freshman wearing glasses stood nearby, looked at the promotional poster on the X-banner, and asked, "Um... can I join?"

Li Hang couldn't even be bothered with recruitment. He picked up an application form and said, "Junior brother, just fill this out yourself."

The young man filled out the form, paid the fee to Guo Caicai, and then stood by watching them play cards.

After getting a rough idea of the rules, the young man asked, "Is this also a regular activity for the animation club?"

"It can be," Chen Guiliang set the tone.

At that moment, he thought of a good idea. After the Legends of the Three Kingdoms cards were printed, he would give a free set to every club at Peking University. And, he could give plenty to the neighboring Tsinghua University as well.

He would turn all these university clubs into his promotional platforms for Legends of the Three Kingdoms!

As noon approached, Zeng Hui said, "You guys keep playing. Sheng Qingchuan and I are going to get lunch."

The two of them were most likely a couple. They left, talking and laughing, taking several lunch boxes with them.

More than one or two people were gathered around watching the card game. Seeing them leave, they immediately sat down. Chen Guiliang simply pulled in three more people for an eight-player game.

"Dismantle!"

"Unassailable!"

"Attack!"

"Eight Trigrams. Haha, I dodged."

"Lightning is in play. Sima, you better watch out."

The game became livelier and livelier. From time to time, passing students would hear the commotion and stop to watch them play.

A young woman asked, "What game is this?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Legends of the Three Kingdoms. It'll be printed and for sale in a while."

Li Hang asked, "What are your requirements for the original art?"

Chen Guiliang replied, "Wei, Shu, Wu, and the Warlords each have their own background color. Wei is blue, Shu is red, Wu is green, and the Warlords are gray. For the character designs, we can reference CCTV's *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*. Oh, senior brother, have you played *Dynasty Warriors* and Koei's *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*?"

"I've played them," Li Hang said.

"We can also draw inspiration from those two games," Chen Guiliang said.

Li Hang smiled. "Those two games, especially Koei's *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*, were also inspired by CCTV's *Romance of the Three Kingdoms*."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Senior brother, how much do you charge for one piece of original art?"

"I don't know."

Li Hang drew for the fun of it and had never been paid before, so he didn't know the current market rate. He taught Photoshop 7.0 drawing skills in the Yuanhuo Club, always for free, and felt awkward about charging money.

Guo Caicai, however, knew the market rates. "Professional artists for magazines like *Comic Fans* get paid about 200 to 500 yuan per piece. For animation companies, original art is 80 to 150 yuan per second. If calculated per frame, it's much lower."

Li Hang felt too embarrassed to charge money, but he did want to earn some. "For the warlord cards, let's say 100 yuan per piece. For the other things like equipment, peaches, and so on, junior brother, you've already drawn them yourself. I'll just help you polish them up, let's say 20 yuan per piece."

"Deal," Chen Guiliang agreed without hesitation.

It was great doing business with university students; they actually offered a lower price on their own initiative.

Chen Guiliang added, "When the Legends of the Three Kingdoms cards are printed, I'll give a set to the Yuanhuo Club and five sets to Senior Brother Li Hang."

"It's a deal!"

Li Hang was especially happy, even happier than when receiving the money.

More and more students gathered to watch them play, so Chen Guiliang gave up his seat.

He and Li Hang exchanged phone numbers, QQ numbers, and email addresses.

"Senior brother, I'll leave this set of Legends of the Three Kingdoms with you for now," Chen Guiliang instructed. "Please get the art done as soon as possible. I'm about to register my company."

Li Hang smiled. "No problem. I'll start researching the TV series and game character models tonight."

Chen Guiliang rode his bicycle to the newly renamed Yannan Canteen. As expected, the rice here was softer than at Canteen No. 1.

Damn it, Chen Guiliang had lost weight again during military training.

He had to start replenishing his nutrients and gain back to at least 140 jin.

After returning the bicycle at Building 28, Chen Guiliang strolled back to his dorm in a cheerful mood.

The last roommate in 404, the "immortal" named Guo Feng, had finally returned from his wanderings.

This guy was wearing a faded, old t-shirt, tall and thin, with a side-parted hairstyle. At this moment, he was sitting in front of his computer, watching a downloaded episode of *Kangsi Coming* and letting out a silly chuckle from time to time.

That strange laugh reminded Chen Guiliang of Guan Zhiqiang.

"This show's quite interesting," Chen Guiliang went over to start a conversation.

Guo Feng glanced at Chen Guiliang and said, "It's a Taiwanese show, just started this year. The download resources are hard to find. I copied it directly from a friend."

"My name is Chen Guiliang, a freshman," Chen Guiliang introduced himself.

Guo Feng said, "I'm Guo Feng, a junior... Hahahaha, Xiao S is hilarious!"

Chen Guiliang's forehead creased with black lines. This legendary immortal was somewhat different from what he had imagined.

Not a hint of otherworldly grace; instead, he was obsessed with a childish entertainment show.

Well, that wasn't a big deal.

When Chen Guiliang was 40, he had watched Ultraman with his relatives' kids during the Spring Festival. He also quite enjoyed BabyBus, finding it more interesting than those mindless, sweet rom-coms.

Senior Brother Min and Jiang Junlai weren't there, so it was just the two of them in the dorm.

Chen Guiliang, trying to make conversation, probed, "I heard Senior Brother Guo has taken a lot of classes?"

"Just picked them randomly, too lazy to plan," Guo Feng continued to stare at the computer screen. "My advisor recommended a few major courses, and I just picked the rest with my eyes closed. They're just to rack up credits anyway."

Chen Guiliang asked, "What are your plans after graduation?"

"Don't know. I still have two years until graduation, why think so far ahead?" Guo Feng picked up his mouse and clicked to watch the next episode.

Chen Guiliang glanced at the course schedule next to the computer. It was Guo Feng's own schedule, another chaotic mess of classes. Based on what Senior Brother Min had said, and combined with this schedule, Guo Feng would probably have an excess of 20 credits by the end of his junior year.

As long as he could finish his thesis, Guo Feng could graduate after his third year.

Just then, Jiang Junlai returned to the dorm, with Yun Fan and Deng Chen from the room across the hall following him.

When the three saw Guo Feng watching the show, they all gathered around to watch too. An IMO winner, a provincial top scorer, and a municipal top scorer were actually watching with great interest.

What was a childish entertainment show in Chen Guiliang's eyes was incredibly novel and exciting to the university students of this era!

Chen Guiliang asked, "Senior Brother Guo, where's a good place to get a computer built?"

"Just call me by my name."

Guo Feng reeled off the information like an expert. "If you want to choose your own components, go to Hailong Building. They have the most complete selection. To buy a pre-built machine, you can go to Pacific Plaza. But at both places, you have to be careful not to get ripped off. Dinghao Electronics City, which opened last year, has to compete with the older businesses, so their prices are more transparent than at Hailong and Pacific."

As he spoke, Guo Feng added, "I suggest you wait a while before buying a computer. Especially next semester, when the seniors are graduating, they'll post on the BBS to sell their computers. The price is usually around 1,000 yuan, and even the best configurations won't exceed 2,000. For lower-performance ones, you can get one for just a few hundred yuan."

Deng Chen asked, "Senior brother, are you very familiar with building computers?"

"I took computer science as an elective and worked part-time at a digital plaza," Guo Feng glanced at the time on his computer. "You guys have a lecture from your advisor this afternoon, right?"

Jiang Junlai said, "Professor Xu Lai's lecture."

Guo Feng said, "His classes are interesting, but very hard to get into, especially *Neo-Confucianism in the Song and Ming Dynasties*. When I was a freshman, I stayed up all night at the computer but still couldn't get in. Later I went to audit the class, but even the audits were often full. If you were a little late, there were no seats."

Chen Guiliang lay down for a nap and said to Jiang Junlai, "Wake me up when it's time."

In his drowsy state, bursts of laughter came from the dorm. The four top students were thoroughly amused by Xiao S.

"Chen Guiliang, time for the lecture!"

After what felt like an eternity, Chen Guiliang was shaken awake by Jiang Junlai.

They all arrived at a large classroom, filled with all the students from the Yuanpei Program, both arts and sciences.

A very young-looking old professor stood on the stage. "Hello, everyone. I've been a strong supporter of Peking University's Yuanpei Program from the very beginning. I know you're all feeling lost right now. I was lost when I was young too... Back then, I was a soldier on the grasslands. I didn't know anything, and I didn't know what I should do in the future. All I had with me were three volumes of *A History of Chinese Literature*. There should have been four, but one was missing for some reason..."

"A person's life is full of many experiences. Every experience is a precious asset. For example, after you choose your courses, you have a two-week trial period. Past Yuanpei students often say that the experience of choosing the wrong course was very valuable. When you choose the wrong course, you learn clearly what you like and what you're suited for. Then, when you apply to your advisor to change courses, you'll study with exceptional earnestness and drive..."

"When I was a soldier on the grasslands, I learned how to make pasta. I was a cook back then, and I've kept that skill to this day. If I have the chance, I'll treat you to noodles I've kneaded myself..."

"My introduction to philosophy began with Lenin..."

This wasn't a serious academic lecture, but rather an attempt to coax freshmen into choosing philosophy courses.

Professor Xu Lai recounted amusing stories from his time as a soldier on the grasslands and mentioned how, when taking the postgraduate entrance exam for Peking University, he wrote "I was very nervous during the exam" at the end of every paper.

The students burst into laughter from time to time as they listened.

"In 1985, I was an assistant to Mr. Feng Youlan. He had just finished writing the Wei-Jin volume of his *New History of Chinese Philosophy*, and I disagreed with some of his analysis. I offered my opinions to Mr. Feng, and he thought I was right, so he accepted them. But later, when the book was published, he changed it back... Everyone has their own thoughts; academic disagreements are very normal. In the future, if you think I've said something wrong, you can also point it out to my face. We can learn from each other..."

After listening to the lecture, the students found it very interesting and decided one after another to sign up for Professor Xu Lai's courses.

But in the following days, all the lectures were very interesting... and they didn't know which to sign up for anymore.

Having too many choices was also a kind of torment.
